correctness.rationale: An independent spherical Wick contraction gives the moment formulas. For the second moment only pairings between the two tensors survive trace-freeness, giving 6t/7!!=2t/35. For the fourth moment the loopless cubic multigraphs on the four tensor copies have opposite-edge multiplicities (3,0,0), (2,1,0), or (1,1,1), up to permuting the three opposite-edge pairs. They contribute 108t², 1944u and 1296v, respectively, divided by 13!!; the count per ordered triple (a,b,c) is (3!)⁴/(a!b!c!)². Writing A_i=(T_ijk)_{jk}, the tetrahedral contraction is v=Σ_ij tr(A_i A_j A_i A_j), and Σ_i A_i²=M by full symmetry. For a traceless 3×3 matrix X, tr(X⁴)=tr(X²)²/2 by Cayley–Hamilton. Taking the coefficient of s² at X=A_i+sA_j and summing over i,j yields 4u+2v=t²+2u, hence v=t²/2−u. The resulting fourth moment is 4(7t²+6u)/5005. Subtraction gives the stated squared Frobenius deficit. For xyz, M=I/18 and the probability-measure moments are 1/105 and 1/5005, so the lower bound is sharp and isotropy is necessary and sufficient.
residual_risks: This reconstructs the result for real cubics in three variables only. It does not classify isotropic tensors into rotation orbits.
